answers.answer: No. Unpurchased reserved cards contribute neither their eight points toward the score or trigger nor their two white bonuses toward costs or nobles. The summary assigns scoring and usable bonuses to purchased cards.
answers.evidence: Prestige Point Sources: 'Printed on each purchased card'; Payment rules: 'bonus from previously purchased development cards'; Noble Visits: 'bonuses (from purchased development cards)'.

answers.answer: You receive no physical blue token. The permanent blue bonus reduces future purchase costs and can satisfy a noble's bonus requirement even though the card gives zero prestige.
answers.evidence: Bonus Stacking: 'Bonuses reduce costs but never generate tokens'; Development Cards: prestige 'may be 0'; Noble Visits require 'bonuses (from purchased development cards)'.

answers.answer: Its own blue bonus cannot pay for itself: purchase discounts come from previously purchased cards, so you cannot afford that purchase. A newly purchased white bonus does count toward a noble at the end of the same turn, because the noble check follows the action and uses bonuses from purchased cards.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: 'Each bonus from previously purchased development cards'; Turn Structure: 'After performing their action ... checks for a noble visit'; Noble Visits: 'bonuses (from purchased development cards)'.

answers.answer: The blue bonuses cover the one blue cost only. The three excess bonuses cannot cover green or create change. You still need two green tokens, with gold able to substitute for either or both.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: 'permanent gem of that color'; Bonus Stacking: 'the excess provides no benefit for that purchase (no "change" is given)'; Gold tokens 'can substitute for any single gem token'.

answers.answer: The bonuses remain permanent and are not used up. If the other noble stays available, taking gems on your next turn can still be followed by receiving that noble at the end of that turn. You cannot collect it during an opponent's turn.
answers.evidence: Bonus Stacking: 'adds exactly one bonus of its color permanently'; Noble Visits: 'At the end of their turn'; 'The other noble(s) remain available for future turns'; 'at most one noble per turn'.

answers.answer: Yes. Reserving a face-up development is allowed without owning tokens, developments or reserved cards, regardless of its level or affordability. The reservation action requires no printed-cost payment and gives you one gold if available.
answers.evidence: Reserve a Development Card: 'Take one development card and place it in your hand'; may reserve 'A face-up development card from the 3x4 grid'; 'Upon reserving, also take 1 gold token'; maximum three reserved cards. Printed-cost payment appears under Purchase a Development Card.

answers.answer: No market card is removed or refilled for a blind reservation from the deck. All twelve market cards remain. You receive only the one reserved card, with no second replacement card in your hand.
answers.evidence: Reserve a Development Card: 'Take one development card'; alternative is 'The top card from any one of the three level decks'; Card Replacement applies when a face-up card is 'purchased ... or reserved from the grid'.

answers.answer: The four face-up cards remain available to purchase or reserve. Purchasing one leaves its space empty for the rest of the game because the deck cannot refill it. The other three stay available.
answers.evidence: Purchase a Development Card: 'Purchase a face-up development card from the grid'; Reserve a Development Card permits a face-up grid card; Card Replacement: 'If the corresponding deck is empty, the empty space in the grid remains empty for the rest of the game.'

answers.answer: The summary gives fifteen prestige as the end-game trigger, but does not explicitly address whether complete development-card exhaustion itself ends the game; that particular exhaustion ruling is unsupported. Its action rules do permit buying an affordable previously reserved card or taking one gem in each of three available different colors.
answers.evidence: End-Game Trigger: 'When any player reaches 15 or more prestige points'; Turn Structure: 'Purchase ... 1 card you reserved on a previous turn'; Take 3 Gem Tokens: 'Take 1 gem token from each of 3 different color piles.' No complete-exhaustion end condition is stated.

answers.answer: Yes. You can temporarily rise from ten to thirteen tokens and return all three newly taken tokens, leaving your holdings unchanged. A net gain is not required by the stated rule.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit: 'may temporarily exceed 10 during their action'; 'may return some or all of the tokens they just took'.

answers.answer: A's two spent gold return to the supply. B can take one when reserving, leaving one gold in the supply immediately afterward, before token-limit returns.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: 'Spent gold tokens are returned to the supply'; Reserve a Development Card: 'Upon reserving, also take 1 gold token'.

answers.answer: Yes. You may buy that face-up level-3 card if you can pay for it. The purchase rule permits a face-up grid development and states no lower-level purchase or unlocking prerequisite.
answers.evidence: Purchase a Development Card: 'Purchase a face-up development card from the grid ... by paying the gem token cost shown on the card.' Setup exposes four cards at each of the three levels.

answers.answer: You cannot skip the noble: its visit is automatic and cannot be refused. You finish the turn with eighteen prestige: twelve plus three from the card plus three from the noble. Players who still have a turn in the current round continue playing to equalize turn counts.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits: 'automatic -- a player cannot refuse it'; 'Each noble tile is worth 3 prestige points'; End-Game Trigger: 'the current round is completed so that every player has played the same number of turns'.

answers.answer: The game ends after D completes that turn. A, B, C and D have then taken the same number of turns, so A does not start another round and nobody receives an additional turn.
answers.evidence: End-Game Trigger: 'the current round is completed so that every player has played the same number of turns'.

answers.answer: No replacement noble is revealed. The seven removed tiles are permanently out of the game. The acquired noble is placed face-up in front of its recipient, leaving two nobles available in the middle.
answers.evidence: Noble Tile Mechanics: 'Noble tiles removed during setup are out of the game permanently'; Noble Visits: 'Place the received noble tile face-up in front of you'; two-player setup reveals three nobles.

answers.answer: Emerald is green, diamond white, sapphire blue, onyx black, ruby red and gold joker yellow. There are ninety development cards: forty level 1, thirty level 2 and twenty level 3.
answers.evidence: Components token table: Emerald/Green, Diamond/White, Sapphire/Blue, Onyx/Black, Ruby/Red, Gold (Joker)/Yellow. Development Cards (90 total): Level 1/40, Level 2/30, Level 3/20.
